evidence:
NESTING (static, these bytes). task.toml:18 `[agent] timeout_sec = 7200.0`; task.toml:21 `build_timeout_sec = 600.0`; task.toml:27 `[verifier] timeout_sec = 13200.0` (3 h 40 min, below the five-hour limit). tests/test.sh:213 `run_suite gates 1500`, tests/test.sh:224 `run_suite scored 11100`, tests/test.sh:207 `timeout "$budget_sec" rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1` (judges run one at a time, so the sum is the right bound). judge.toml line 4 in each dimension: render `timeout = 600`, constraints `timeout = 600`, functional `timeout = 9000`, polish `timeout = 900`, visual `timeout = 900`. Arithmetic: gate judges 600 + 600 = 1200 < 1500 (300 s slack); scored judges 9000 + 900 + 900 = 10800 < 11100 (300 s slack); budgets 1500 + 11100 = 12600 < 13200 (600 s slack). Liveness: test.sh:116-122 loops 120 times with `sleep 0.25` and a 2 s per-URL urlopen timeout (test.sh:50), nominally 30 s and at the extreme about 120 x (2+2+0.25) = 510 s for a port that accepts and hangs, still inside the 600 s slack outside the suites. Restart: restart_mcp.py:11 `HELPER_TIMEOUT_SEC = 55` covers the helper's 5 s kill wait plus 30 s nominal readiness loop; single use, so it costs the 9000 s functional judge at most 55 s. All of these values are byte-identical to the frozen template: tests/test.sh, tests/tools/restart_mcp.py, tests/tools/score.py, tests/Dockerfile and tests/scoring.toml compare equal to rules/projects/webdev-task-template, and task.toml differs from the template only in identity/metadata lines (name, description, keywords, difficulty, difficulty_explanation, category, provenance, arena_slice); the template judge timeouts are the same 600/600/9000/900/900. No timeout was raised, so no authorization record is needed. They also match the reference in staged-task-contract.md:111 (`gates 1500, scored 11100, verifier 13200`).

SUFFICIENCY. Agent build: environment/Dockerfile is a slim Node image with one apt layer and two global npm packages; hosted environment_setup took about 15 s (10:10:27 -> 10:10:42, likely cached) against 600 s. solve.sh only checks for open DB handles and copies a prebuilt app (`cp -a "$source_app/." "$target/"`), oracle agent_execution about 1.4 s against 7200 s. Workload on these bytes: 1 render + 2 constraints gate criteria, 42 functional, 6 polish, 3 visual criteria (counted from the frozen judge.toml files). Only timing evidence for a configured judge is the hosted Oracle run on an EARLIER candidate (41 functional criteria): result.json verifier started_at 2026-10-02T10:10:47.879726Z, finished_at 2026-10-02T10:52:12.660962Z = about 2485 s for verifier image setup plus all five judges, against a 12600 s combined suite budget; app-restart.log `app-restart pid=1961 ready=1 at 2026-10-02T10:30:56Z` shows the functional judge was mid-run about 20 min in; exception_info None, graded 1. That is roughly 5x headroom overall and at least 3.6x for functional even if all 2485 s were attributed to it.

WHAT IS NOT MEASURED (reason risk=true). No configured judge run exists for these bytes (raw-evidence-index scope says so). The export records no per-judge durations, so the margin of the three short timeouts (render 600, constraints 600, polish 900 for six criteria including a 390 px resize-and-reload criterion, visual 900) is not individually known even on the earlier candidate; only that each finished without timing out there. Since then the render gate was changed (reduced to load-and-type, which shrinks it), one functional criterion was added and several criteria reworded, so the earlier total is supporting evidence, not a measurement. Scripted golden duration is not judge duration and is not used here. A weak or slow submission (target-model app) could make the judge spend longer than the golden did; no scored-suite run on a model app exists (the only model run stopped at the render gate). Verifier-image build time (tests/Dockerfile installs Chromium with deps, claude-code, codex) against any build limit is not separately recorded, though it completed in the hosted run.

ADVERSARIAL TRY. Broken app that could pass: none relevant to this row; a slow or hanging app cannot gain reward from a timeout because test.sh writes zero first and `run_suite` failure exits with the zero/gate record. Conforming alternative that could fail: a correct app on which the polish judge needs more than 900 s for six criteria would be zeroed for the whole scored suite (test.sh:224-226 `if ! run_suite scored 11100; then exit 0`), an evaluator failure attributed to the submission; this is a template-wide property, not shown to occur, and the earlier hosted run finished all scored judges without it.
